name: Sanctions & coercion
value: US blockade of Iran; Graham Act in force
summary: US naval blockade of Iran continues; lifting it is central to Iran's terms
state: The US naval blockade of Iranian ports remains in force; Iran's plan to reopen Hormuz requires the US to lift sanctions and end the blockade, and Iran called the US reply unconvincing on 4 Nov (Al Jazeera). The Russia and Iran sanctions act signed in October expands secondary sanctions and tariff powers against trading partners (Baker McKenzie). No major economy has been cut off from payment systems.
for_you: Firms trading with Iran, Russia or their partners face expanded compliance risk. Check official OFSI and OFAC guidance.
rubric_hit: Blockade and secondary-sanction threats on large economies = Watch

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Iran says US reply to Hormuz plan unconvincing
Baker McKenzie — US President signs Russia and Iran sanctions bill with new tariff powers

why: Sanctions are now a frontline weapon; secondary sanctions and asset seizures fragment global finance and trade.
drivers: Russia/Iran sanctions packages, secondary sanctions, frozen-asset decisions, export controls.

rubric.alert: Major economy cut off from payment systems, or large-scale seizure of sovereign assets.
